finding: tests/test_signal_search.py:223 The combined filter test does not discriminate eight required filters.
rationale: AC3 requires every supplied facet to constrain results, but the sole filter test combines all nine while severity="high" alone uniquely selects signal-alpha, every projected review state is hard-coded to "unreviewed", and no other test exercises filters, so an implementation ignoring the other eight facets would pass.

evidence.output: Acceptance criterion: "Filter by detector, group or category, severity, source, table, run, date, and review state when supplied."

The fixture has signal-alpha severity high, signal-beta severity low, and signal-gamma severity medium. Lines 223-232 submit detector_id, group, category, severity, source_id, table_id, run_id, date, and review_state together; lines 236-237 assert only ["signal-alpha"]. Thus severity="high" alone produces the asserted result even if the other eight filters are ignored.

All search_signals callsites are in tests/test_signal_search.py; only the call at lines 221-223 supplies filters. The remaining calls exercise lexical queries, pagination, or stale projection behavior without filters.

The projected payload sets review_state to "unreviewed", and the projection tuple independently stores the literal "unreviewed" for every signal. The existing matching review_state assertion cannot distinguish applied filtering from ignored filtering; a nonmatching value is required.

Canonical production emits detector_id, table_id, source evidence, status, severity, run_id, and provenance executed_at, but no review_state; the search projection derives review_state. No canonical-producer guard makes any of the eight untested filter predicates unreachable.
